title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 1 (Short Title, Extent, Commencement and Application)

content.overview: Section 1 of the Companies Act, 2013 provides the short title, extends the Act to the whole of India, provides for phased commencement of provisions by Central Government notification, and defines the categories of companies and body corporates to which the Act applies, including carve-outs where special legislation is inconsistent.
content.glance: State the short title; note all-India extent; explain phased commencement by notification; list the application categories in s. 1(4) and the special-Act inconsistency carve-outs.
content.study: Section 1 is the gateway provision of the Companies Act, 2013. Sub-section (1) gives the short title. Sub-section (2) extends the Act to the whole of India. Sub-section (3) brings s. 1 into force at once and authorises the Central Government to notify different commencement dates for different remaining provisions; a reference to commencement of the Act in any provision is read as a reference to the coming into force of that provision. Sub-section (4) applies the Act to (a) companies incorporated under this Act or any previous company law; (b) insurance companies (except inconsistency with the Insurance Act, 1938 or IRDA Act, 1999); (c) banking companies (except inconsistency with the Banking Regulation Act, 1949); (d) electricity generation/supply companies (except inconsistency with the Electricity Act, 2003); (e) any other company governed by a special Act (except inconsistency with that special Act); and (f) such body corporate incorporated by any Act as the Central Government may notify, subject to specified exceptions, modifications or adaptations. Current-law framing: always check the specific notification bringing a provision into force and any special-Act inconsistency before applying a Companies Act section.

sections.heading: Short Title
sections.body: Section 1(1): This Act may be called the Companies Act, 2013.

sections.heading: Extent
sections.body: Section 1(2): The Act extends to the whole of India.

sections.heading: Commencement
sections.body: Section 1(3): Section 1 comes into force at once. Remaining provisions come into force on dates appointed by Central Government notification; different dates may be appointed for different provisions. A reference to commencement of the Act is construed as a reference to the coming into force of that provision.

sections.heading: Application — Companies and Special Entities
sections.body: Section 1(4) applies the Act to companies under this Act or previous company law; insurance, banking and electricity companies subject to special-Act consistency; other special-Act companies subject to consistency; and notified body corporates with specified adaptations.

sections.heading: Special-Act Carve-Outs
sections.body: Where the Companies Act is inconsistent with the Insurance Act, Banking Regulation Act, Electricity Act or another special Act governing the company, the special Act prevails to the extent of inconsistency.

provisions.title: Short title, extent, commencement and application

examples.title: Phased commencement
examples.body: A provision of the Act is challenged as applicable on a given date. The analysis must identify the Central Government notification (if any) bringing that provision into force under s. 1(3).

examples.title: Banking company inconsistency
examples.body: A provision of the Companies Act conflicts with a mandatory provision of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 applicable to a banking company. Under s. 1(4)(c), the Banking Regulation Act prevails to the extent of inconsistency.

examples.title: Previous company law company
examples.body: A company incorporated under the Companies Act, 1956 continues to be governed by the 2013 Act under s. 1(4)(a), subject to transitional and savings provisions elsewhere in the Act.

hypotheticals.question: Does every provision of the Companies Act, 2013 apply from the date of Presidential assent?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Only s. 1 itself came into force at once; remaining provisions require Central Government notification under s. 1(3).

hypotheticals.question: Does the Companies Act override the Banking Regulation Act for banking companies?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 1(4)(c) applies the Companies Act only except in so far as its provisions are inconsistent with the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

hypotheticals.question: Can the Central Government apply the Act to a statutory body corporate?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes, under s. 1(4)(f), by notification, subject to such exceptions, modifications or adaptations as may be specified.

misconceptions.trap: The entire Companies Act, 2013 came into force on a single date.
misconceptions.correction: Section 1 came into force at once; other provisions were brought into force by phased notifications under s. 1(3).

misconceptions.trap: The Companies Act always overrides sectoral statutes for banks and insurers.
misconceptions.correction: Section 1(4) expressly preserves special-Act provisions to the extent of inconsistency.

misconceptions.trap: Only companies incorporated under the 2013 Act are covered.
misconceptions.correction: Section 1(4)(a) also covers companies incorporated under any previous company law.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 1 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. State short title and extent. II. Identify whether the relevant provision has been notified under s. 1(3). III. Test application under s. 1(4) and any special-Act inconsistency. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions on s. 1 contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Notification status of the provision; entity category under s. 1(4); special-Act consistency analysis if applicable; precise relief.
